findings.message: `domain::AdrBaselineCheckOutcome::Blocked` exposes `violations: Vec<AdrBaselineCheckViolation>` publicly, so callers can construct `Blocked { violations: vec![] }` directly. The `blocked()` constructor therefore cannot enforce the documented non-empty invariant; use a non-empty collection type or a private wrapper.

`usecase::AdrBaselineService::execute` combines mutating `Snapshot`/`Restore` commands with non-mutating `CheckReview`/`CheckCommit` queries returning a check read model. Split the command and query contracts/interactors so callers and implementations do not depend on both sides.

All four CLI argument DTOs carry `items_dir`, but `cli_driver::AdrBaselineInput` has no corresponding field and `AdrBaselineCompositionRoot` accepts only `project_root`. A custom items directory therefore cannot cross the CLI→driver→composition boundary. Preserve it in the mirror chain or document and type an explicit lossless conversion.

`usecase::AdrBaselineStorePort` exposes ledger entries but no operation or documented guarantee for verifying that each referenced verbatim baseline copy still exists and matches its ledger hash. Consequently the check contract cannot enforce AC-03 against a deleted or modified copy; `MissingBaseline` merely declares vocabulary without naming an enforcement owner.

`working_bytes` and `fork_point_bytes` return `Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, AdrBaselineError>`, while `AdrBaselineError::SourceUnavailable(AdrSourceFileName)` also represents unavailable source bytes. With no documented distinction, `None` and `Err(SourceUnavailable)` overlap and adapters can encode the same state inconsistently.

`AdrBaselineSourcePort` performs filesystem/Git reads and `AdrBaselineStorePort` performs filesystem persistence, but every method is synchronous and neither entry acknowledges the blocking execution choice. The port contract should explicitly justify synchronous I/O or declare the appropriate async color.

Both secondary ports return the shared six-variant `AdrBaselineError` without documenting producible subsets. Source reads cannot structurally produce `Store`, `InvalidReason`, or primary-adapter filename-validation failures; store operations likewise cannot produce source-reader and primary-adapter variants. Use port-specific errors or document precise per-method subsets.

`decode_ledger_line` and `encode_ledger_entry` return `AdrBaselineCodecError`, whose `Io` and `Transaction` variants cannot be produced by these pure string codecs. The entry docs do not declare a producible subset, forcing callers to handle structurally unreachable failures.

`cli_driver::TrackIdInput::try_new`, `AdrSourceFileNameInput::try_new`, and `AdrBaselineReasonInput::try_new` return broad shared errors. Each constructor can produce only its own validation subset, but the declarations neither use precise errors nor document those subsets.

The docs for `domain::AdrBaselineKind`, `domain::AdrBaselineLedgerEntry`, `domain::AdrBaselineSourceState`, and `domain::AdrSourceFileName` restate CN-01–CN-04/AC-06–AC-07 behavior such as reason requirements, fork-point selection, draft exemption, and path restrictions. Replace these restatements with short identifying phrases and anchor references.

The docs for `usecase::AdrBaselineSourcePort`, `usecase::AdrBaselineStorePort`, and `usecase::AdrBaselineInteractor` reproduce upstream behavior including fork-point reads, atomic append, mechanical restore, reason legality, and draft exemption. Keep the behavior in spec.json and cite its anchors instead.

The docs for `infrastructure::adr_baseline::{decode_ledger_line,encode_ledger_entry}`, `infrastructure::FsAdrBaselineStore`, and `infrastructure::FsGitAdrBaselineSource` restate CN-01–CN-04/AC-02/AC-07 behavior, including append-only encoding, collision handling, merge-base reads, and draft classification.

The docs for `cli_driver::AdrBaselineInput`, `AdrBaselineReasonInput`, and `AdrSourceFileNameInput` restate upstream reason-permission, non-empty-reason, and ADR-path validation behavior instead of referring to CN-02/CN-03/AC-06.

The docs for `cli::AdrBaselineCheckCommitArgs`, `AdrBaselineCheckReviewArgs`, `AdrBaselineCommand`, `AdrBaselineRestoreArgs`, and `AdrBaselineSnapshotArgs` reproduce AC-04/CN-02/CN-05 behavior such as fail-closed entry checks, atomic snapshots, and latest-copy restoration. Replace the prose restatements with anchor-based identification.

`cli_composition::AdrBaselineCompositionRoot::new` returns the broad `CompositionError`, but the declared construction chain uses only infallible adapter, interactor, and driver constructors. Variants such as `ConfigLoad`, `Usecase`, and `Infrastructure` therefore have no structural origin, and the docs specify no reachable subset. Return `Self` or declare the actual fallible step and precise error subset.

The `as_str(&self) -> &str` signature is duplicated across `TrackIdInput`, `AdrSourceFileNameInput`, `AdrBaselineKindInput`, and `AdrBaselineReasonInput`; `try_new(String) -> Result<Self, AdrBaselineValidationError>` is also duplicated across the source-name and reason inputs. These sibling `add` entries should share contracts such as `AsRef<str>` and `TryFrom<String>` or a local trait.
findings.category: duplicated method signature across sibling types

findings.message: `FsAdrBaselineStore` and `FsGitAdrBaselineSource` duplicate the exact sibling constructor `new(PathBuf) -> Self`. Declare a shared construction contract such as `From<PathBuf>` instead of repeating the public signature.
findings.category: duplicated method signature across sibling types

findings.message: `AdrBaselineLedgerRecordDto.docs` restates the upstream ledger wire contract by enumerating `source/hash/kind/reason/timestamp`. The catalogue field shape and `spec_refs` already carry that information; retain only a short role phrase and anchor references to avoid a second behavioral SoT.

`AdrBaselineInteractor` and `AdrBaselineQueryInteractor` duplicate the exact constructor taking `Arc<dyn AdrBaselineStorePort>` and `Arc<dyn AdrBaselineSourcePort>`. These sibling `add` entries should share a dependency value or constructor trait rather than repeat the same contract.
findings.category: duplicated method signature across sibling types

findings.message: `AdrBaselineQueryService::execute` exposes the full `AdrBaselineQueryError`: a valid query cannot produce `AdrBaselineStoreError::Write`, and source unavailability is already modeled as the fail-closed `AdrBaselineCheckViolation::SourceMissing` rather than an operational query error. The docs specify no subset, so callers must handle unreachable leaves. Use a query-specific read error or document and enforce the exact mapping.

`AdrBaselineStorePort` combines the query-only `read_entries`/`verify_recorded_copy` group with the command-only `snapshot`/`restore` group. The separate command and query interactors consequently depend on methods they must not use. Split read/verification and mutation ports; the filesystem adapter may implement both.

`AdrBaselineCommand::Snapshot` and `AdrBaselineStorePort::snapshot` both admit every `kind + Option<reason>` combination, but no entry names the sole AC-06 enforcement owner. `AdrBaselineReasonInput` cannot enforce the rule because it cannot see `kind`, while the store port cannot return `AdrBaselineValidationError`. Assign the interactor or another capable layer as the exactly-one owner of required/forbidden-reason rejection.

`cli::commands::adr_baseline::dispatch` declares `Result<cli_driver::CommandOutcome, CliError>`, but input construction is infallible and `AdrBaselineCompositionRoot::execute` already returns a plain `CommandOutcome`; consequently every `CliError` variant is structurally unreachable. Return `CommandOutcome` directly or add a genuine typed failure path.

`cli_driver::AdrBaselineInput` represents both pre-composition and post-composition states: every variant permits `track_id: None`, and `Snapshot` also permits `timestamp: None`, while `AdrBaselineDriver::handle` accepts this same type even though the use-case command requires resolved values. Thus unresolved requests are valid driver inputs and require runtime rejection. Split the unresolved composition request from a resolved driver input with required `TrackIdInput`/`Timestamp` fields.

The ADR baseline adapter reads metadata/spec files with `fs::read_to_string` without first rejecting symlinks. A symlink under `track/items/<track_id>` can redirect the adapter outside the repository and is followed at the I/O boundary; enforce `symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` rejection as required by the infrastructure convention.

Ledger and snapshot-copy reads do not reject symlinks before following them (`read_to_string`, `read_dir`/`read`, and `fs::read`). A malicious symlink in the baseline directory can redirect verification/restoration or ledger parsing to an unrelated file; perform explicit symlink checks at the boundary and fail closed.

`append_ledger_line` opens the ledger with `create(true).append(true)` without checking `symlink_metadata`. If `ledger.jsonl` is replaced by a symlink, the append follows it and writes outside the baseline directory, violating the required real-file semantics and append-only trust boundary.

`atomic_overwrite` restores to `root/knowledge/adr/<source>` without rejecting a symlink at the target boundary. `fs::rename` can replace the symlink itself, but a symlinked parent directory can redirect the write outside the trusted repository root; validate the target path and every relevant parent component before restoring.

Metadata and spec loads do not reject symlinks before `read_to_string`, allowing repository-controlled paths to redirect reads outside the intended workspace. Apply explicit `symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` rejection at this boundary.

Baseline ledger and recorded-copy reads follow symlinks without boundary rejection. A symlinked ledger or snapshot can redirect parsing or verification to unrelated files; reject symlinks before `read_to_string`/`read`/directory traversal.
`append_ledger_line` opens an existing `ledger.jsonl` with append mode without checking whether it is a symlink, so a replaced ledger symlink can redirect writes outside the baseline directory.

`AdrSourceFileName` は `C:outside.md` のような Windows drive-relative prefix を許容するため、Windows ではこの `join` が `knowledge/adr` を捨てて trusted root 外を指し得ます。`reject_symlinks_below` は包含関係を検証しないため、working-tree 読み取り前に Windows prefix を拒否し、解決後のパスが root 配下であることを確認してください。
snapshot copy 名と restore target の組み立ても、`C:outside.md` のような source により Windows 上で project root 外へ逸脱できます。symlink guard だけでは防げないため、scope-config loader のパターンと同様に prefix 拒否と trusted-root 包含検証が必要です。

versioned schema である `metadata.json` を、`schema_version` を持たず `deny_unknown_fields` もない部分 DTO に直接 deserialize しています。未知の将来版や legacy/余剰フィールドを黙って切り捨て、その `base_branch` で merge-base を計算してしまうため、既存の `track::codec::decode` のように version envelope を先に検証して strict DTO を使用してください。

`user_decision_ref` の有無を YAML の行頭文字列で判定しているため、flow mapping や quoted key として記述された有効な field を見落とし、昇格済み ADR を draft と誤分類して刻印要求から除外できます。逆に block scalar 内の同名 prose は誤検出します。検証済みの parsed front-matter 構造から field presence を判定してください。

ledger hash の prefix に一致する最初のファイルを返すため、仕様上サポートされる hash8 collision では、別 hash の短い名前も候補に一致します。`read_dir` 順序次第で verification が誤って mismatch になり、restore は別 snapshot の bytes を書き戻してデータを破壊できます。候補を full SHA-256 で照合してから選択してください。
working-tree ADR は `fs::read`、fork-point ADR は `Command::output` で無制限にメモリへ読み込まれます。repository-controlled な巨大 ADR により snapshot/check がメモリ枯渇し得るため、両経路に同一の明示的な byte 上限と typed error を設けてください。

append-only で増え続ける ledger 全体を無制限に `String` と `Vec<AdrBaselineLedgerEntry>` へ読み込んでいます。通常運用による肥大化や細工された ledger で restore/check がメモリ枯渇し得るため、ledger bytes・line length・entry count を上限付きで読み、超過時は fail-closed にしてください。
`find_copy` は full hash が一致したファイルだけを返すため、改変された copy は `None` となり、ここでは `HashMismatch` ではなく `Missing` と報告されます。その結果 `HashMismatch` 分岐は到達不能です。候補ファイルの存在と内容照合を分離し、候補が存在して hash が異なる場合は実際の hash を返してください。
`snapshot` は `MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` を検査せず copy と ledger を正常記録できますが、同じ adapter の verify/restore はその copy を上限超過として拒否します。成功した書込みが直後から読めない状態を作るため、書込み前に snapshot bytes の上限を fail-closed で検証してください。
読取り側には ledger 全体・行長・entry 数の上限がありますが、append 側はどの上限も検査しません。長大な reason、10,001 件目、または 8 MiB 超過の append が成功して ledger を以後読めない状態にするため、copy 作成前に現在量と追加 record を検証してください。

baseline directory の `read_dir` を entry 数の上限なしで最後まで走査します。directory は workspace input であり、無関係な大量ファイルを置くだけで verify/restore の I/O と実行時間を無制限に増やせます。ledger 上限に対応する scan 上限を設け、超過時は typed error で fail-closed にしてください。

対応対象 hash と異なる全候補を mismatch として保持するため、正規の hash8 collision で長い prefix 側の copy だけが欠落した場合、短い prefix を所有する別 hash の正常な copy を `HashMismatch` と誤報します。その候補自身の full hash が filename label と整合するなら collision sibling として除外し、対象 copy は `Missing` と判定してください。
ledger 上限の検証と append が同一クリティカルセクションではありません。上限直前で複数の snapshot が並行すると、双方が検証を通過してから append し、entry 数または byte 上限を超えた読取り不能な ledger を生成できます。排他ロック下で再検証と append を一体化してください。

`Snapshot` 入力と `AdrBaselineStorePort::snapshot` に timestamp がなく、唯一の production adapter が内部で `timestamp_now()` → `chrono::Utc::now()` を呼んでいます。同一の usecase 入力が暗黙の時計に依存し、Usecase Layer Purity Rules の「時刻は entrypoint の引数として渡す」に違反します。`Timestamp` を command／port 引数へ追加し、composition root で取得してください。

`check` embeds the AC-07 stamp-eligibility policy directly in the usecase layer by deciding that `Init | Cite` qualifies an existing ADR and `Init | NewAdr` qualifies a promoted track-born ADR, then branching on `AdrBaselineSourceState`. These are domain decisions, not orchestration. Move the eligibility/state policy behind domain methods or a domain value and let the interactor only collect port results and emit violations, per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §Usecase Layer Purity Rules and §CLI as Composition Root.
GO-01 の「可視化できる」という明示的な目標意図を、完了時に決定論的に証明する AC がありません。AC-02/AC-05 は累積記録と復元・briefing を定めていますが、init 版と最終版などの baseline 差分を review/PR で可視化できることを検証していないため、目標の一部が未カバーです。
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: `TrackBornPromoted` incorrectly treats an `Init` record as satisfying the required stamp. AC-07/D7 requires a promoted track-born ADR to be stamped through `new-adr` (including its mandatory reason), while `Init` is reserved for the primary ADR at track initialization. Returning `true` for `[Init]` suppresses `MissingRequiredStamp` and bypasses that fail-closed invariant; accept only `NewAdr` for this state and update the corresponding test.

Snapshot/Restore では write 用、CheckReview/CheckCommit では read 用の track-id 解決を選択し、別の TrackCompositionRoot 呼び出しと再パースまで CLI 内で行っています。これは単一の typed Input を Driver に渡す範囲を超えた分岐・多段オーケストレーションです。`knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root の境界に従い、未解決の track-id と操作種別を driver/usecase 側へ渡してください。

`project_root_from_items_dir` が `items_dir` の構造を解釈・検証し、adapter 用 project root を算出しています。このアプリケーション固有のパス変換と分岐は thin-bin の責務外です。`items_dir` をそのまま composition/driver 境界へ渡し、`knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root に沿って request-scoped wiring 側で解決してください。

The `init` record contains `"reason":null`, but the ledger contract and briefing require `reason` to be absent for kinds other than `new-adr` and `escalation`. Fix the machine serializer to omit a missing reason and regenerate this ledger entry.

The snapshot command left an unignored runtime lock file in the current diff, although the baseline artifact contract contains only the snapshot copy and `ledger.jsonl`. Do not commit this coordination sidecar; ignore `*.jsonl.lock` or place the lock outside the tracked baseline directory.

The checkout step does not set `fetch-depth: 0`, so the workflow still performs a shallow clone. Track-aware CI's `adr-baseline check-commit`/fork-point resolution can therefore fail when the base branch history is unavailable, contrary to the stated CI fix.

`init` は primary ADR filename を必須入力に変更したが、既存の `plan` workflow は feature name だけで `init` を呼び、`adr2pr` も自身の ADR 入力を渡していない。このままでは正規の複合フローが branch/metadata 作成後の snapshot で失敗し、部分初期化状態を残す。両 caller から選択済み ADR filename を明示的に引き渡す必要がある。

新しい ADR-baseline 経路が `/track:diagnose` adapter と同期していない。adapter は依然 `rollback-diagnoser` のみを dispatch し、旧 `routing_target` schema だけを返す一方、SSoT は `adr-diagnoser` verdict と snapshot/restore を要求する。さらに同じ SSoT の Constraints/Outputs は mutating subcommand と file modification を禁止したままであるため、実行者がどちらに従っても文書化された recovery を完遂できない。adapter と diagnose-only/recovery-write 境界を同時に更新すべきである。

ADR semantic freeze は非任意の framework review methodology だが、consumer-owned の `.harness/custom/` severity policy に置かれている。これは `knowledge/conventions/responsibility-boundary.md` の「framework methodology は custom に置かない」という境界に反し、consumer の severity customization で凍結規定まで消せる。凍結規定を framework-owned reviewer contract/prompt に移し、custom file は severity preferences に限定する必要がある。

`adr2pr` の唯一の引数は primary ADR filename だが、呼び出し先の `/track:init` が必須とする feature name の取得元が adapter/SSoT のどちらにもない。「feature context と共に渡す」とだけ記載されているため、新規 track の Step 1 は `/track:init <feature> --primary-adr <file>` を構成できない。さらに README の正規フローは依然 `/track:adr2pr` を引数なしで呼んでいる。feature と ADR を含む一貫した invocation contract を定義し、README と init forwarding を同期する必要がある。

`/track:diagnose` は inline の diagnostic input を受け付ける一方、この adapter は briefing の作成を禁止している。しかし `bin/sotp capability exec` は非空の `--briefing-file` が必須であり、SSoT も caller-provided briefing のみを使用する。このため、pre-existing briefing を持たない直接の user invocation や inline input はどちらの diagnoser も起動できない。command 外で必ず briefing を作る caller contract に限定するか、read-only capability dispatch 前の scratch briefing 作成を adapter/orchestrator の責務として復元すべきである。

The pre-review gate no longer verifies the uniquely selected primary ADR. Invoking `check-review` without `--primary-source` succeeds whenever the ledger contains any `init` record, while `snapshot --kind init` permits multiple source filenames. An unrelated/additional init can therefore let review start even when the intended primary ADR lacks its init snapshot, contradicting the single primary selected by `/track:init`. Preserve the exact primary-source wiring or fail closed when init sources are ambiguous.

This guardrail now claims that the pre-review check derives the primary ADR from plural init records and removes the documented override, but the current Makefile, review adapter/workflow, `CLAUDE.md`, and track-lifecycle convention still require exactly one init source and support `ADR_BASELINE_PRIMARY_SOURCE`. Restore the singular/override wording or co-update the actual wiring; the current rule contradicts the harness contract.

The review wrapper still drops the exact primary ADR identity required by D4/AC-04. In derived mode, `check-review` only requires that some `init` record exists; `init` can also appear for additional sources, so an unrelated init record can satisfy this gate while the orchestrator-selected primary ADR has no init snapshot. Rewording every document as a “primary set” does not restore the required check. Preserve/derive the uniquely selected primary source and pass `--primary-source`, or otherwise persist and validate that identity fail-closed.

The workflow SSoT now describes a plural primary set and says `--primary-source` is direct-CLI-only, but the current Claude adapter, Makefile wrapper, CLAUDE.md, README, and conventions still derive exactly one init source and support `ADR_BASELINE_PRIMARY_SOURCE` at the wrapper. This breaks adapter–SSoT synchronization and gives different operational contracts depending on which surface is read. Align this workflow with the existing singular/override wiring or co-update the other surfaces and implementation.

The convention now replaces the single orchestrator-selected primary ADR with a set inferred from every init record. The no-argument CLI path only requires that at least one init record exists, so a stray init for another source can satisfy the pre-review gate while the intended primary lacks its snapshot. This contradicts the immediately preceding single-primary contract and D4/AC-04’s fail-closed requirement. Preserve and validate the exact primary source rather than redefining all init records as primaries.

This convention says `check-review` verifies exactly the init-designated source set, but the current query validates every ledger entry/copy and byte-compares every recorded source against its latest baseline; the init set only supplies the required-presence condition. Consequently a cited/new-ADR source mismatch can block review even though these docs assign non-primary coverage to the commit gate. Document the actual split: require a nonempty init designation set, while byte-validating all recorded ADRs.

This still says the pre-review CLI verifies exactly the init-record source set, directly contradicting `review-protocol.md`, which now correctly states that the init set is only the presence requirement and every recorded ledger copy/source is also byte-validated. The guardrail, review adapter/workflow, CLAUDE.md, and Makefile descriptions retain the same stale “exactly init records” contract. Propagate the corrected two-part semantics across all surfaces.

Provider-neutral SSoT が Phase 0 の起動形式を Claude 固有の `/track:init ...` と規定しています。一方、Codex adapter は sub-workflow を `$track-init` で起動すると定義しており、SSoT 冒頭の「provider-specific invocation framing は adapter に置く」という契約にも反します。ここでは feature と primary ADR filename の受け渡しだけを規定し、具体的な起動構文は各 adapter に残してください。

T001 contains upstream design-contract restatements (filename validation, kind/reason legality, append-only semantics, source state, and byte-check violations). Keep the task description to target + operation + anchor cites.
T002 restates upstream behavior (permitted source bytes, draft exemption, and fail-closed error preservation) instead of limiting the description to target + operation + anchor cites.

T003 contains extensive upstream contract restatements (atomic snapshot/ledger writes, preservation and collision rules, merge-base citation, draft classification, deterministic byte comparison, and latest-copy restore).
T004 restates the input-validation behavior contract (validation of untrusted track ID, filename, kind, and reason) rather than only naming the target, operation, and anchors.
T005 restates the diagnostic and exit-status behavior contract (structured/sanitized diagnostics and status handling) beyond the permitted target + operation + anchor form.
T006 restates the out-of-scope strictness invariant (preserving adr_user evaluator and signal-gate strictness) in prose; cite OS-01/AC-09 without re-litigating the upstream contract.
T007 restates the diagnoser's behavioral routing contract and prohibition on direct ADR/baseline edits. The task should name the target files/sections, operations, and anchors only.
S1 restates upstream design rationale/behavior ('approved domain model and fail-closed vocabulary'); plan sections must contain executable sequencing and anchor references, not contract prose.
S2 restates upstream layer/dependency rationale ('secondary adapters implement the established ports and invariants') rather than only sequencing tasks with anchors.

S3 restates the downstream dependency rationale ('rebuild ... before downstream gate wiring depends on the new commands') in the plan section; keep this as a dependency/order statement with task references, not a design-contract restatement.
S4 restates operational policy rationale ('diagnoser and reviewer/fixer policy are active when a mismatch is found') instead of limiting the section to task ordering and anchors.

T004 explicitly cites IN-03, CN-04, and AC-04 in its description, and its attributed CLI entries implement those anchors, but the corresponding coverage arrays omit T004. Reconcile these mappings so task completion remains traceable.

T006 names only `Makefile.toml` precisely; “the track-init workflow” and “the affected maintainer, README, convention, verification-gate, and hook documentation” leave several possible files and provider adapters. Enumerate the exact targets so the executor does not have to invent the task boundary.

T006 is the sole task mapped to AC-09 and owns the workflow wiring needed by AC-04/AC-07, but it contains no validation step. The component tests in earlier tasks do not verify invocation from review, guarded commit, and track-aware CI or confirm that signal-gate strictness remains unchanged. Add explicit gate-wiring and unchanged-strictness verification.

T007 is the only task mapped to AC-08, yet its explicit targets cover the diagnoser and ADR reviewer prompt only. “Affected workflow documentation” neither identifies the fixer instruction/capability contract required by AC-08 nor supplies a validation step, so the task could complete without establishing the mandated fixer prohibition. Name the applicable fixer targets and verification explicitly.

T006の「Verify the init snapshot is required before review...」以降は、AC-01/AC-04/AC-07/AC-09 の期待挙動を task 内で文単位に再記述している。`knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` に従い、正確な対象ファイル、検証操作、anchor cite だけに縮めること。

T007の「ADR meaning must not change...」および verdict ごとの検証説明は、IN-04/IN-06/CN-05/AC-05/AC-08 の挙動契約を散文で再記述している。`knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` に従い、対象ファイルへの clause 追加と focused verification の操作を anchor cite で指定する形にすること。

`task-coverage.json` maps AC-04 to T004, but T004 only implements the CLI/primary-adapter command boundary and argument validation. It does not wire or validate the review-entrance, guarded-commit, and track-aware CI enforcement required by AC-04; that work is described in T006. Remove T004 from AC-04 unless the task description is expanded with an actual AC-04 validation step.

T003 is a split candidate: it combines the Git source adapter, filesystem store, ledger codec, and regression tests. Its current `libs/infrastructure/` implementation is about 1,459 lines—nearly 3× the configured 500-line ceiling—so it is not an individually committable within-ceiling task. Split the source-adapter work from the store/codec work and their tests.

`execute` converts project-root and track-resolution failures directly into `CommandOutcome::failure` (here and at line 37), placing user-facing stderr rendering in the composition root. Keep these failures typed and let `cli_driver`/the CLI boundary map them to output.
D3 は刻印ごとに新しい複製を追加すると規定していますが、ファイル名が `<slug>.<hash8>.md` のみなので、同一内容の再刻印や hash8 衝突時には既存名と衝突します。下流 spec は再利用・失敗・別名生成のどれを受入条件にすべきか導出できません。刻印 identity と衝突時の意味論について amendment proposal による裁定が必要です。

D6 は `reason` を5値 enum（init/cite/new-adr/non-semantic-fix/escalation）と規定する一方、直後に escalation の根拠 ref を `reason` に記録すると要求しています。D3 の ledger schema に別の ref field はなく、下流 spec は enum 値と任意 ref を同時に表現できません。ledger/CLI の表現を amendment proposal で裁定する必要があります。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D1 は baseline を「user が最後に承認した文面」と定義していますが、D6 は grounding escalation による adr-editor 編集後、user 承認を前提にせず直ちに working tree を刻印すると規定しています。この snapshot が D1 の承認済み baseline なのか、別の authorized baseline なのかを下流 spec が確定できません。escalation 刻印の承認境界について amendment proposal による裁定が必要です。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: Amendment proposal: D1 states that legitimate D5/D6 re-stamped baselines await final user approval at merge, but D3 still calls every accumulated version approved, and D5 (line 88) calls the latest restored bytes user-approved. After an escalation snapshot, the latest baseline is intentionally still pending approval, so downstream spec cannot assign it a consistent trust state. Distinguish the initially approved anchor from authorized-but-pending re-stamps while preserving the chosen latest-copy restore behavior.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D1 は baseline を「user が最後に承認した文面」と定義し、Rejected B もそれを唯一の錨としていますが、D7 は未承認（🟡）の自発起草 ADR を `new-adr` として即時刻印します。承認済み文面が存在しない ADR も baseline になり得るため定義が矛盾しています。semantic-freeze に従い、許容される未承認 baseline の信頼状態を明示する amendment proposal として user 裁定が必要です。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D4 は review scope に含まれる全 ADR file の刻印を要求しますが、Neutral は凍結対象を track が cite する ADR のみに限定し、無関係 ADR は write-scope 可視化だけに委ねるとしています。`adr` scope は `knowledge/adr/**` の変更をすべて含むため、無関係 ADR を block・刻印するのか対象外にするのかを downstream spec が一意に導出できません。semantic-freeze に従い amendment proposal として対象集合を裁定する必要があります。

findings.message: 自発起草 ADR は `review_finding_ref` により 🟡 となり strict merge gate で停止しますが、user の非同期裁定後に front-matter をどう 🔵 へ昇格し、どの snapshot kind で再刻印して gate を再開するかが未定義です。既存規約では `user_decision_ref` を追加するだけでは `review_finding_ref` が残る限り 🟡 のため、この遷移なしでは merge lane が閉じたままです。downstream spec が実装可能な承認昇格フローを導出できるよう、semantic-freeze に従い amendment proposal として user 裁定が必要です。

`AdrBaselineDriver::handle` duplicates the kind/reason semantic legality check (`requires_reason` versus `reason.is_some()`) in the primary adapter. This is business logic that the briefing states is owned by the use-case interactor; the driver should only map the typed input, invoke the single service, and render its result.

`handle` routes `Snapshot`/`Restore` to `command_service` and `CheckReview`/`CheckCommit` to the separate `query_service`, so this primary adapter branches between interactors based on the request variant. Inject one aggregate application service and delegate each request through that single boundary, as required by `hexagonal-architecture.md` §Usecase Layer Purity Rules.
findings.category: handle not delegating to single use case

findings.message: The wildcard arm makes `handle` validate composition state instead of performing only input → invoke → render. It also misreports `Snapshot { track_id: Some(_), timestamp: None, .. }` as a missing track ID. Since composition owns resolving both optional fields, pass a resolved-only input to the driver so this state is unrepresentable, per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §Usecase Layer Purity Rules.
